why: Maximum remaining power = 100 minus the cheapest top-to-bottom falling path, where each step goes down-left, down or down-right. That is the classic minimum falling path sum, a row-by-row 2-D DP.
hints: Maximising remaining power is the same as minimising total cost. What does the cheapest way to reach a cell in row i depend on?
best[i][j] = city[i][j] + min(best[i-1][j-1], best[i-1][j], best[i-1][j+1]) over existing columns.
Fill row by row (keep only the previous row), answer = 100 - min(last row). O(rows * cols); brute force is also fine for 4x4.
pitfalls: Edge columns have only two predecessors.
The drone pays for the starting cell too.
The result can be negative; do not clamp at 0.
